cases.title: Fix XaiModel streamed text after a native tool call being merged into the ended pre-call part
protected_invariants: Text streamed after a native tool call remains a distinct live part and reaches final output.
A delta is never applied to a part whose lifecycle already ended.
cases.discrimination_reason: A one-line provider adapter change crosses stream part identity, native-tool boundaries, CallToolsNode semantics, and retry exhaustion; a coarse model/provider tag is expected to over-select sibling xAI behavior.
cases.notes: Direct upstream commit with explicit pre-fix failure explanation and focused regression tests.

cases.title: Keep a run cancelled during its first tool call resumable
protected_invariants: Cancellation during the first or only tool call records an interrupted request even when no tool completed.
Interrupted history synthesizes missing tool returns and can resume with or without a new prompt.
cases.discrimination_reason: The blast radius crosses abnormal termination, tool lifecycle, persisted message state, provider-valid history repair, and future resume semantics rather than a single path-local function.
cases.notes: Oracle names are taken from the upstream regression patch; exact source URL is canonical if upstream later moves tests.

cases.title: Fix DeferredToolRequests.remaining resolving cross-category result IDs
protected_invariants: An approval result can resolve only an approval request with the same ID.
A call result can resolve only a deferred call with the same ID.
A cross-category result cannot resume the model or execute an external call.
cases.discrimination_reason: The safety property is semantic category ownership of an ID; file or component tags cannot explain why a same textual ID in a different result category must not authorize progress.
cases.notes: Small focused production diff plus explicit no-external-call regression oracle.

cases.title: Fix stale UIEventStream part state on cancellation
protected_invariants: Synthetic PartEnd emitted on cancellation reflects all deltas already exposed to the client.
Cleanup errors do not replace the original stream failure.

oracle.notes: Upstream commit carries parametrized text, thinking, function-tool and native-tool cases. Amendment A1 corrected the oracle path from nonexistent tests/ui/test_event_stream.py to canonical tests/test_ui.py; test names and protected behavior were unchanged.

cases.discrimination_reason: The invariant depends on temporal correspondence between emitted deltas and synthetic cleanup state, not merely the UIEventStream component membership.
cases.notes: Same broad stream family as #7925; family-aware analysis prevents overweighting correlated cases. Amendment A1 is recorded on issue #18 comment 5525636969 and was made before Gate B baseline freeze or any BIG execution.

cases.title: Fix dropped zero-argument tool calls in CohereModel
protected_invariants: Falsy None or empty-string arguments do not cause a valid named zero-argument tool call to be dropped.
The zero-argument tool call survives the assistant/tool history round trip without a retry prompt.
cases.discrimination_reason: A generic truthiness check changes provider parsing, tool execution, retry behavior, and request-history validity; the protected behavior is narrower than a Cohere model tag.
cases.notes: Very small production change with extensive upstream regression coverage.

cases.title: fix(flows): pair a function response with the call it answers
protected_invariants: A reused function-call ID pairs each response with the newest preceding owning call.
Multiple progress responses for one call retain the final update without stealing a later call's response.
cases.discrimination_reason: Correctness depends on ID plus temporal ownership and call ordering. A static flow tag cannot encode which repeated-ID relation is safe.
cases.notes: Direct upstream commit with three explicit repeated-ID oracles.

cases.title: fix: deliver parallel sub-agent failures to the caller
protected_invariants: A parallel sub-agent failure reaches the caller even when the merged generator is suspended at yield.
A branch that fails before emitting an event cannot appear successful.
cases.discrimination_reason: The bug is an async control-flow interaction between branch task lifetime, queue signaling and generator suspension, broader than the modified ParallelAgent lines but narrower than all parallel-agent tests.
cases.notes: Both Python 3.11+ and pre-3.11 merge paths are covered upstream.

cases.title: fix: honor before_run_callback early-exit for Workflow runs
protected_invariants: A before_run callback that returns Content terminates Workflow execution with that Content, matching the non-workflow contract.
Early-exit output is persisted without starting the workflow root node.

tests: workflow before_run callback Content early-exit regression cases

cases.discrimination_reason: The same callback contract spans workflow and non-workflow execution paths; component-only mapping is likely to miss contract equivalence or over-select all runner behavior.
cases.notes: Larger runner refactor than most cases; retained with medium confounding risk.

cases.title: fix: prevent duplicate synthetic user event on single-turn agent resumption
protected_invariants: Resuming from an HITL tool confirmation does not inject a synthetic user event that shadows the user's FunctionResponse.
A confirmed single-turn tool request does not enter an infinite confirmation loop.
cases.discrimination_reason: The failure crosses persisted HITL state, resume inputs, synthetic-message injection and confirmation lifecycle; its infinite-loop consequence is not captured by a local input-preparation tag.
cases.notes: Direct upstream commit; source URL is canonical for exact test location.

cases.title: fix(a2a): Promote RemoteA2aAgent response to workflow node output
protected_invariants: A terminal RemoteA2aAgent textual response becomes the workflow node output consumed by downstream JoinNode aggregation.
Partial, non-final, thought-only and input-required events never claim the single workflow output slot.

oracle.notes: Upstream report also documents a real multi-agent A2A workflow E2E reproduction.

cases.discrimination_reason: The impact path crosses remote-agent event semantics, terminal-state filtering, Context.output ownership, workflow completion and JoinNode aggregation.
cases.notes: Narrow agent-boundary production fix with substantial focused tests.

cases.title: fix: stop tracing credentials passed via config.http_options
protected_invariants: Credential-bearing http_options fields never reach exported LLM request trace attributes.
Non-sensitive http_options such as base_url remain traceable.
cases.discrimination_reason: A tracing serializer change carries a security invariant about free-form credential channels; selecting all tracing tests is safe but coarse, while skipping sibling telemetry blindly is not auditable.
cases.notes: Sentinel-secret upstream oracle directly asserts absence from serialized trace data.

cases.title: fix: do not mount a cluster credential into the GKE code sandbox
protected_invariants: A pod executing model-generated code has automount_service_account_token=false and therefore does not receive the cluster service-account credential.
cases.discrimination_reason: The changed manifest field is tiny, but the invariant belongs to the trust boundary between untrusted model-generated code and Kubernetes credentials; it should map to sandbox security evidence, not every GKE executor behavior.
cases.notes: Selected over ADK 550189... because this commit protects one critical invariant with very low confounding risk.

cases.title: fix(core): preserve serialized approval resume ownership
protected_invariants: Current-response generated-item ownership survives serialization so a later-turn approval can resume safely.
Released-schema or malformed ownership that cannot prove the response boundary fails before approval-tool execution.

oracle.notes: Upstream parametrizes streamed/non-streamed, session/no-session and mixed tool positions, and checks fail-closed malformed ownership.

cases.discrimination_reason: The invariant is identity/provenance across serialized state and approval authorization. It is not equivalent to all HITL or all session behavior and is a strong skip-proof challenge.
cases.notes: Larger change retained because the upstream oracle explicitly proves both safe resume and fail-closed non-execution.

cases.title: fix(sessions): apply the reasoning item id policy to stored session history
protected_invariants: reasoning_item_id_policy=omit applies to stored history on read as well as newly written items.
A revoked historical rs_* identifier cannot be replayed into a later model request and cause a 404.
cases.discrimination_reason: The policy must hold across write, read, replay, handoff and streamed/non-streamed paths. Static file mapping either misses cross-path consistency or selects most of session handling.
cases.notes: Oracle simulates the real Responses API 404 for a revoked reasoning item ID.

cases.title: fix: redact JSON validation errors
protected_invariants: Payload-bearing JSON validation errors exposed to callers, logs or traces do not retain sensitive input data through messages, run_data, cause/context or traceback frames.
Redaction is preserved across streamed, realtime, handoff and final-output error propagation paths.
cases.discrimination_reason: This is an intentionally difficult cross-cutting privacy case: the protected invariant propagates through exception lifetimes rather than one module. BIG must remain conservative; high confounding risk is reported, not hidden.
cases.notes: Large cross-cutting change. Kept because it independently labels a critical security invariant that should punish false-safe selection.

cases.title: fix(sessions): recover failed resumed Session writes before model calls
protected_invariants: A failed or cancelled resumed-session append remains pending across serialization and is reconciled before the next model call.
Recovery never reruns already completed tools and fails closed when authoritative history is changed or ambiguous.
A failed underlying Session mutation invalidates stale compaction cache state.

tests: resumed Session write recovery, ambiguity rejection, serialization and streamed/non-streamed regression cases

cases.discrimination_reason: The invariant spans durable checkpoint state, uncertain backend acknowledgement, exact-history reconciliation, model-call ordering and no-reexecution semantics.
cases.notes: Family-aware scoring prevents three session/resume cases from being treated as independent evidence of the same mapping capability.

cases.title: fix(memory): preserve reusable scope configs
protected_invariants: Validating or normalizing memory scope/slice configuration does not mutate caller-owned mappings.
The same configuration object can be reused with identical semantics.
cases.discrimination_reason: The diff is local but the protected behavior is aliasing/ownership across multiple future constructions. A path rule sees validators; the semantic invariant is caller-state immutability.
cases.notes: Small, focused, low-confounding state-mutation case.

cases.title: Fail closed when human-feedback emit cannot classify
protected_invariants: Human-feedback emit routing does not silently choose emit[0] when classification cannot be performed or matched.
Unclassifiable feedback raises HumanFeedbackCollapseError; an explicit empty-skip default remains distinct from classification failure.
An unspecified collapse LLM resolves through project model configuration instead of a hard-coded provider.
cases.discrimination_reason: This is a release-policy-grade fail-open/fail-closed invariant spanning LLM resolution, classification and graph routing. It directly tests whether impact selection understands consequence rather than file adjacency.
cases.notes: Coherent multi-file change retained at medium confounding risk because the central safety invariant is explicit.

cases.title: Persist custom conversational replies after fallback append
protected_invariants: A public string returned by a custom @listen route is persisted after the fallback assistant append so a fresh Flow instance restores the assistant turn.
Built-in converse does not double-append and message-added events remain exactly once per user/assistant turn.
cases.discrimination_reason: The bug is caused by ordering between graph kickoff persistence and a post-kickoff fallback append; semantic timing, not path membership, determines the impacted restore contract.
cases.notes: Docs churn is excluded from the semantic label; production behavior is focused.

cases.title: fix: refuse dispatch cycles and bound dispatch depth in the Studio dispatch tools
protected_invariants: Self-dispatch and A-to-B-to-A cycles are refused using runtime lineage rather than prompt convention.
Dispatch depth is bounded and malformed or partially present reserved lineage metadata fails closed.
Caller-writable metadata cannot forge or reset reserved dispatch lineage/depth state.
Team/workflow cancellation can cascade to registered dispatched sub-runs.

oracle.notes: Upstream commit records explicit pre-fix baselines and mutation verification.

cases.discrimination_reason: A highly cross-cutting adversarial case: lineage provenance, cycle detection, depth policy, metadata sanitization and cancellation span multiple dispatch surfaces. High confounding risk is intentional to test conservative widening on critical behavior.
cases.notes: 837 gated tests and 28 targeted mutations are reported upstream; this case is weighted by family and confounding risk rather than allowed to dominate.

FunctionCallingConfig mode reaches LiteLLM tool_choice semantics.
